answer: Submission rate is limited to 8 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole army of identities from one uplink. An operator running many aliases therefore forfeits for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the sable quota and the comet admission check. Because the counters live in the beacon ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
